solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One achieving great success across the board

definitions.text: One achieving great success across the board

parts.words: One achieving great success across the board
parts.note: Surface reading: a person who succeeds in every field, 'across the board' meaning everywhere at once.
Setter's reading: the board is a chessboard, and the great success is the top title in chess.

explanation.surface: Praise for an all-round high achiever who wins at everything they try.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across the board' is an idiom for 'in every area'; read literally it is play over a chessboard, where the highest title is GRANDMASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The top title awarded by the world chess federation goes to players of the highest international ranking.

clue.text: Shine having got work in market town

parts.note: a shine or lustre on a surface
OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone who has found a job in a country town and is glowing about it.
explanation.walkthrough: GLOSSOP is a market town in Derbyshire, in the north of England, on the edge of the Peak District.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this Derbyshire place has held a weekly trading day for centuries.

clue.text: A second layer of a pale hue

parts.note: the article kept as it is
S is the standard abbreviation for a second of time
a hen is a bird that lays eggs, so a layer

explanation.surface: A decorator describing a second coat of paint in a pale colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' looks like a coat of paint but is read as 'one who lays': a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes a grey, drained colour like wood ash, so it works as an adjective for a pallid tint.

clue.text: Get rid of one blemish between successive days

indicators.note: 'one blemish' sits between the two 'days', so those day letters wrap round it

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day; the first of the two successive days
the Roman numeral for one
a scar is a mark that spoils the skin
the second day of the pair, another D

explanation.surface: Advice on removing a spot that appeared one day and was gone the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Successive days' supplies two Ds, one on each side of the inner pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard something is to throw it away or abandon it, a close synonym of dispose of.

clue.text: Leo and Adam done up in the latest fashion

indicators.note: to do something up is to rework or refashion it, so the two names are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of both names, 'and' simply joining them

explanation.surface: Two men, Leo and Adam, dressed up in the newest styles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' is part of the fodder's joining, not a letter source: only the names are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase is borrowed into English meaning stylish or current, matching a phrase about present-day style.

clue.text: Tragic girl drinking wine beginning to notice its pleasing quality?

indicators.note: the girl takes the wine into herself when drinking it, so she goes round it

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles, Thomas Hardy's tragic heroine
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

indicators.note: the beginning of 'notice' means only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of 'notice'

explanation.surface: A heroine sipping wine and starting to appreciate how good it is.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy's Tess is the crossword's stock tragic girl. The question mark flags that 'its' refers back to the wine in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Tastiness is the quality of having a good flavour, the pleasant quality a wine offers the drinker.

clue.text: In tirade a member of the house is unrestrained

indicators.note: the member is placed in the tirade, so the tirade's letters surround it

parts.note: a rant is an angry, ranting speech
a Member of Parliament sits in the House of Commons
the article kept as it is, placed after the member

explanation.surface: A politician losing control while shouting a furious speech in the chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The house' is the House of Commons, so its member is an MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampant means spreading or behaving without check, a synonym of unchecked, wild or uncontrolled.

clue.text: This fellow beset by idiots and duds

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded, so the idiots close in round this fellow

parts.note: clots are fools
the pronoun for this male person

explanation.surface: A man surrounded by fools and failures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duds' looks like more failures to go with the idiots, but it is slang for garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Duds is informal slang for garments or outfits, so it names what one wears.

clue.text: Firm undertakes to make room for a thousand concessions

indicators.note: the firm and its undertakings part to make space for the thousand to go between them

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
to undertake is to promise
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A company agreeing to accept a thousand deals or allowances in a negotiation.
explanation.walkthrough: The thousand slots in where the firm meets its undertakings.
explanation.definitionFit: A compromise is a settlement where each side gives something up, so plural concessions matches plural compromises.

clue.text: When facing problem, journalist may be taken in

parts.note: 'as' can mean 'when', as in 'as I left'
a sum is an arithmetic problem
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter facing trouble who might be fooled or conned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' looks like 'deceived', but here it means taken on or adopted, as a name or manner is assumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Assumed means adopted or put on, as with a false name or air; taken on board is the sense used.

clue.text: Battleship has got a hundred at sea

indicators.note: being all at sea means confused, so the letters are in disorder

parts.note: all eleven letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A warship notching up a century of voyages out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits the naval surface so well that it hides its role as the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Dreadnought gave its name to a whole class of big-gun early twentieth-century warships.

clue.text: Fellow's thus held to be a craftsman

indicators.note: the fellow has 'thus' held, gripped inside him

parts.note: a fellow is a man; the 's reads as 'has'
'so' means 'in this way'

explanation.surface: A man being judged by his skill as a craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow's' is 'fellow has', so the man has 'thus' held within him.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason is a skilled worker who builds with stone, one kind of craftsman.

clue.text: Hate a man to be getting agitated about independence

indicators.note: the stirred letters go round the letter for independence
something agitated is stirred up, so the letters of 'a man to be' are shaken into a new order

parts.note: all the letters of these four words
I is the abbreviation for independent or independence

explanation.surface: A man getting worked up over a campaign for independence and coming to hate it.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of 'a man to be' wraps round the I.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe or detest intensely, a stronger synonym of the verb meaning dislike.

clue.text: Was model again rested?

parts.note: the prefix RE- means again
a model posed for an artist or camera

explanation.surface: A question whether a model, sitting a second time, was really taking a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Again' comes after 'was model' in the clue but its letters come first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Reposed means lay at ease or took a break, a formal synonym of the past tense verb.

clue.text: Jazz fan rhythmically talks up American slave

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means read from bottom to top, so the jazz fan and his talk turn round

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
rapping is speaking in rhythm over a beat
US is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A jazz lover rapping in praise of an American enslaved person.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'jazz fan rhythmically talks' turns round; the American is added at the end unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartacus was the gladiator who led the great revolt of enslaved people against Rome in 73 BC.

clue.text: Put up before court, first pair of defendants turned round

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
CT is the abbreviation for court

indicators.note: the chosen pair from 'defendants' is flipped to face the other way
only the opening two letters of 'defendants' are wanted

parts.note: a letter selection: the opening two letters taken from 'defendants', not an abbreviation

explanation.surface: Accused people put on trial, with the first two defendants spinning round in the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up before court' reads as one legal phrase, but 'put up' is the definition and 'before' is ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Erected means built or raised upright, as a tent or wall is put up.

clue.text: Between two thoroughfares see a duck

indicators.note: the lone letter sits between the two roads, which flank it

parts.note: a mall is a broad walk or street, as in The Mall in London
the article kept as it is
RD is the abbreviation for road, the second thoroughfare

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's tip: look between two streets and you'll spot a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link word, as in 'look, a duck'.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallard is the common wild duck with the green-headed male, a specific kind of the bird.

clue.text: Lethargy of monkey with nothing to eat

indicators.note: the monkey eats nothing, so it takes the zero inside itself

parts.note: the langur is an Asian leaf monkey
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A monkey listless from having no food.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's hungry monkey explains the tiredness, but the monkey actually swallows the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Languor is a pleasant or weary sluggishness, a close synonym of listlessness and inertia.

clue.text: Characters hemmed in by joy-rider angered, put into confusion

indicators.note: the letters wanted are enclosed by the words that follow, lying inside them

parts.note: runs from the end of 'joy-rider' into 'angered'

explanation.surface: A furious joy-rider, boxed in by police, left in a state of confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the D of 'joy-rider' and stops before the final D of 'angered'.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into disorder or madness, the sense of unsettling or disturbing.

clue.text: Travel across estate accompanying a quiet police force

indicators.note: the travelling word stretches across the other pieces, one letter on each side

parts.note: to go is to travel
EST is the abbreviation for estate
the article kept as it is
P, for piano, is the musical mark for quiet

explanation.surface: Travelling over a country estate alongside a discreet police unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accompanying' just places the pieces side by side inside GO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was the secret state police of Nazi Germany, a notorious specific force.

clue.text: Get busy with fight south of Indian state

parts.note: Goa is a small state on India's west coast
a bout is a boxing or wrestling match

explanation.surface: Starting a fight somewhere below a state in India.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'south of' means placed below, so the fight comes after the state.
explanation.definitionFit: To go about a task is to set to work on it or tackle it, the same phrasal sense.

clue.text: Rebel Jack interrupting little woman in school

indicators.note: the rebel breaks into the woman's name, splitting it

parts.note: Amy is one of the March sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women
Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450

explanation.surface: A rebellious boy called Jack disrupting a small girl at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little woman' is not a small woman but one of Alcott's Little Women; 'Jack' is the rebel's first name, not a sailor or card.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a school or place of training, a common synonym for an educational institution.

clue.text: Health resorts in which one finds a saint or a drunk

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about unsteadily, so the letters reel into another order

parts.note: the letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Spa towns where you might meet either a holy person or a boozer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A drunk' looks like a noun paired with 'a saint', but 'drunk' is the shuffle signal acting on 'a saint or a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanatoria, the Latin plural of sanatorium, are establishments for convalescence and treatment of the chronically ill.

clue.text: Sound conveyed by historic languages

indicators.note: the words that follow carry the letters within them

parts.note: the tail of 'historic' plus the start of 'languages'

explanation.surface: A sound passed down through ancient tongues.
explanation.walkthrough: It spans the final C of 'historic' and the opening of 'languages'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a loud metallic ringing noise, one particular kind of noise.

clue.text: A bit cold? Then dance endlessly!

indicators.note: without its end, the dance loses its final letter

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
the rumba, a Cuban dance, with its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: Feeling a little chilly? Get up and dance to warm up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit cold' reads as 'slightly cold', but 'A bit' is the definition and 'cold' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumb is a tiny fragment, as of bread, so it is a small piece or morsel.

clue.text: After first course of meal Conservative makes a dash

parts.note: soup is often served as a starter
CON is the abbreviation for Conservative, the British party

explanation.surface: A Tory politician rushing off after the starter at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the Conservative behind the first course. 'A dash' looks like a sprint but is a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupçon, from French, is a very small quantity or trace, like a hint or touch of flavour.

clue.text: Let up on struggling to get rich

indicators.note: something struggling is thrashing about, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: all seven letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Advice to ease off on striving if you want to become wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let up on struggling' reads as one phrase, but 'struggling' acts on the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means wealthy or lavishly luxurious, a synonym of affluent and well off.

clue.text: When put out, Percy bleats in a socially accepted manner

indicators.note: someone put out is upset, disturbed, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: all eleven letters of the name and the verb

explanation.surface: A man named Percy who complains politely when annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' suggests annoyance in the surface; as a signal it means disordered.
explanation.definitionFit: Respectably means properly and decently, conforming to standards of conduct that society approves.
